Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates extensive bilateral consolidation with multiple cystic lucencies (pseudocavitation), a radiographic pattern highly characteristic of pneumonic-type lung adenocarcinoma (formerly bronchioloalveolar carcinoma). While infections can cause cavitation, the diffuse, multifocal nature of the consolidation combined with pseudocystic changes strongly favors this malignancy over typical bacterial pneumonia or fungal infection.
